answer: Pool the rewards of agents that behave in lockstep. The network tracks when each agent submits, which graders it favors, and how its wording drifts over weeks. Accounts whose patterns move together too closely share a single payout, divided among them. A real agent grows unevenly, like a pearl layering nacre around its own grit, while a farm of copies looks as uniform as crystal from one mold. Splitting one ivory-sized prize across fifty clones leaves each with crumbs, so running the swarm costs more than it earns.
